title: Reported Speech with Konjunktiv I
summary: Reporting statements neutrally with Konjunktiv I and appropriate substitute forms.
whyItMatters: Konjunktiv I marks information as reported and lets writers maintain distance from a source without automatically questioning it.

mentalModel.title: Report, do not endorse
mentalModel.content: Konjunktiv I signals that a statement belongs to another speaker.

mentalModel.title: Keep the form recognizable
mentalModel.content: When Konjunktiv I is identical to the indicative, use an unambiguous Konjunktiv II substitute where appropriate.

ruleBlocks.title: Build the present forms
ruleBlocks.content: Use the verb stem plus -e, -est, -e, -en, -et, -en; sein has sei, seiest, sei, seien, seiet, seien.

ruleBlocks.title: Adjust person and reference words
ruleBlocks.content: Change pronouns, possessives, time, and place expressions to fit the reporting situation.

ruleBlocks.title: Use substitute forms deliberately
ruleBlocks.content: For ambiguous plural forms, use Konjunktiv II or würde plus infinitive when it makes the report clearer.

tables.title: Reported Speech Patterns
rows: Die Autorin sagt, sie werde weiterarbeiten.

examples.de: Die Regisseurin erklärte, der Film beruhe auf persönlichen Erfahrungen.
examples.en: The director explained that the film was based on personal experiences.

examples.de: Der Kritiker schrieb, die Figuren seien überzeugend entwickelt.
examples.en: The critic wrote that the characters were convincingly developed.

examples.de: Die Veranstalter teilten mit, sie würden das Gespräch später veröffentlichen.
examples.en: The organizers announced that they would publish the discussion later.

commonMistakes.wrong: Use Konjunktiv I without changing ich or heute.
commonMistakes.correct: Adapt person, time, and place references to the reporting context.
commonMistakes.reason: Reported speech changes perspective as well as verb mood.

commonMistakes.correct: Read it primarily as a marker of source distance.
commonMistakes.reason: Skepticism must usually be signaled through context or wording.

comparisons.summary: Cultural reporting provides authentic statements by artists, institutions, and critics.
Reviews use reported speech to represent other interpretations fairly.
